injection_strategy: Two coupled regressions in the redirect handler, in two distinct logical layers of the same file: (A) onResponseStart adds 307 and 308 to the 301/302 method-change branch, so those redirects wrongly downgrade POST to GET and drop the body; (B) the cleanRequestHeaders call passes a hardcoded false instead of statusCode === 303, so a 303 redirect no longer strips Content-* request headers.
file_count_justification: Defect is one file because redirect method/body policy and the request-header cleanup policy both live in lib/handler/redirect-handler.js, but they are two independent layers (the onResponseStart transition logic vs the cleanRequestHeaders header policy). A fix to only one layer passes the visible test and ~80% of hidden checks but fails the other layer's checks (<0.9 gate).
partial_fix_traps: Fixing only the 307/308 method/body branch leaves 303 Content-* stripping broken (3 checks fail).
Fixing only the 303 header cleanup leaves 307/308 body/method broken (4 checks fail).
Handling only the redirect type named by the symptom leaves the others failing.
expected_failure_summary: Gold 16/16; both-facets-broken 9/16; fix-A-only 13/16 (0.81); fix-B-only 12/16 (0.75) — both partial fixes fall below the 0.9 hidden gate.
